relations.subject: tls:node-to-node-encryption
relations.evidence: The level of encryption imposed on inter-node communications within the cluster can be configured.

relations.subject: tls:cluster-encryption-level
relations.evidence: The cluster encryption-level can only be configured after cluster encryption itself has been _enabled_: see [Node-to-Node Encryption](../clusters-and-availability/node-to-node-encryption.md).

relations.subject: tls:loopback-interface
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - adjective-style predicate, same shape family as the already-promoted exemptFromMemoryQuota, for the one stated exception to strict cluster encryption
relations.evidence: Note, however, that after `strict` has been specified, communication that occurs entirely on a single node using the _loopback_ interface (whereby the machine is identified as either `::1` or `127.0.0.1`) is still permitted in non-encrypted form.

relations.subject: tls:min-tls-version-setting
relations.object: per-service basis, overriding the server-wide default
relations.evidence: You can set the minimum version of TLS that Couchbase Server accepts either for the entire server or on a per-service basis.

relations.subject: tls:min-tls-version-setting
relations.evidence: Couchbase Server 7.6 and later do not support TLS versions 1 and 1.1\.

relations.subject: tls:legacy-tls-versions
relations.evidence: Support for these earlier versions was deprecated in Couchbase Server 7.2\.

relations.subject: tls:min-tls-version-setting
relations.evidence: You can choose to set the minimum TLS version to either 1.2 or 1.3.

relations.subject: tls:cipher-suite-preference
relations.object: server preference (default, recommended) or client preference
relations.evidence: The server's preference is strongly recommended to be used, since secure: however, preference can be delegated to the client, if required.

relations.subject: tls:cipher-suite-preference
relations.object: per-service value, falling back to the global value, falling back to the server default
relations.evidence: If no cipher-suite preference value has been specified for a given service, and a value has been specified globally, the service uses the global value.

relations.subject: tls:cipher-suite-list
relations.object: a per-service custom list, else a global custom list, else a default HIGH-security list
relations.evidence: If no custom list of cipher-suites is established for a given service, and no global list is established, the service uses a list of HIGH security cipher-suites.

relations.subject: tls:cipher-suite-list
relations.evidence: However, only the _Cluster Manager_, the _Data Service_ and the _Analytics Service_ support the custom-configuration of TLS 1.3 ciphers

relations.subject: tls:tls-handshake
relations.evidence: When a TLS connection is established between a client application and Couchbase Server — for example, using the secure port `18091` — a _handshake_ occurs, as defined by the [TLS Handshake Protocol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport%5FLayer%5FSecurity#TLS%5Fhandshake).

relations.subject: tls:hsts
relations.evidence: Only the _Strict-Transport-Security_ header is supported.

relations.subject: tls:console-access-setting
relations.object: HTTP, HTTPS, or both, disabled cluster-wide
relations.evidence: This can be disabled, for the whole cluster; over either HTTP or HTTPS, or over both.

relations.subject: tls:cipher-suite-list
relations.object: TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 present in the custom list, when HTTP/2 is used with TLS 1.2
relations.evidence: If the HTTP/2 protocol is to be used with TLS 1.2, the cipher-suite `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` must be specified in any custom list.

relations.subject: tls:cipher-suite-list
relations.object: HTTP/2 negotiation, when the required TLS 1.2 cipher-suite is absent from the custom list
relations.evidence: If this cipher-suite is _not_ present, HTTP/1 or HTTP/1.1 are used, instead of HTTP/2\.

notable_absence.finding: The page documents encryption scope, versioning, and cipher configuration in detail but never once discusses the performance or latency cost of enabling on-the-wire encryption (node-to-node 'all', or 'strict' mode) - a natural operational question ('what does turning this on cost me?') that native-encryption-at-rest-overview.md answers for its own feature (selective bucket-level encryption specifically to limit overhead) but this page's equivalent network-encryption feature does not address at all.

cross_component_finding: This page uses the bare, unqualified word 'services' repeatedly ('A service can be any of the Couchbase Server Services; it can also be the Cluster Manager') to enumerate what TLS/cipher settings apply to, then separately in the TLS 1.3 section names 'the Cluster Manager, XDCR, and Views' as also TLS-capable but explicitly not services. This is the same architectural pattern the Capella metrics-reference page states for capella:cluster-manager/capella:xdcr ('Metrics are provided for all Couchbase Services, and also for the Cluster Manager and XDCR') - independently confirmed here on a completely separate, self-managed-Server-only page. Minted server:cluster-manager and server:xdcr rather than reusing the Capella concepts (no page states the equivalence), but this is the strongest evidence yet in the registry that the Services/not-a-Service split is a real server/ architectural fact that Capella's monitoring docs are simply surfacing, not a Capella-specific category.
cross_product_finding: None found specific to this page beyond the Cluster Manager/XDCR parallel already noted as a cross-component finding (it happens to also be cross-product, since the parallel concept lives in capella:*).
